title: Unit – 5 : Session – 10 : SLO – 2  |  Integrating Backend Logic with Event Responses
sections: 1. Example of backend logic — a function that computes a result without touching the GUI, e.g. def add(a, b): return a + b, or a database query / file-processing routine.
2. Showing results on a label — the event handler calls the backend function and updates the widget: result_label.config(text=str(add(2, 3))) — the label refreshes immediately on screen.

3. Why integrate logic with events — so user actions drive real computation: the interface stays responsive and each interaction (click, input) produces meaningful output, separating presentation (GUI) from computation (backend) for cleaner, testable code.
